pitch_detail.notes: Opening pitch is a left-trending slab and corner system, or a start from the pedestal and up over the crest. Ends below a golden inverted tooth of rock that marks the crux of the route. Reported grade of this pitch varies between 5.6 and 5.7 depending on the start chosen.

The crux of the original line: a strenuous move left through a thin crack, then back right through dark rock and up a flaring 5.7 groove. Variations exist here, including a jam-and-lieback crack past a flake and a harder 5.9 option.
Stay left of the crest to an obvious notch. From there a 5.5 scramble, a slanting 5.8 fist crack, or a short 5.9+ undercling traverse (easily protected) finishes the technical climbing.

review.changed: Wrote only pitches 1, 4 and 5, which search summaries of these pages agree on. Page fetches were blocked (403 / domain check), so no full belay-by-belay text was read; pitches 2, 3, 6, 7 omitted because pitch numbering varies by party and variations differ. No rappel table: the descent is a walk-off toward Amphitheater Lake or the Southwest Couloir, which has one short rappel.
review.other_findings: Sources count anywhere from 6 to 7 pitches (9 with a newer direct start). Stored descent is empty: walk-off east to Amphitheater Lake / Glacier Canyon Trail, or the Southwest Couloir with a short rappel.

pitch_detail.notes: Third pitch of the Remorse start; reaches the ledge from which Outer Space departs.
Begins up a hard crack, then makes the exposed finger-crack traverse to the right before moving up to the belay. This is the well-known pitch of the route.

Move left from the belay on easy but exposed face moves to a right-facing corner on the right side of a rock pedestal. Climb the corner and shift to the left side of the pedestal to belay. Belaying further left on the pedestal's left side leaves more rope for the next pitch.

A long crack pitch leaving from the left side of the pedestal to a good ledge, about 150 ft. Reports differ on the grade: one account puts it at 5.7+, another calls the start a 5.9 finger crack that widens and eases to 5.8 and 5.7 climbing.
More crack climbing for roughly 160 ft to a belay leaving a scramble of about 50 ft to the top. One account puts a 5.9 move at the start with 5.7 above; another rates it far easier.

review.changed: Used search-result summaries only (page fetches blocked). Wrote pitches 3-7; pitches 1-2 (Remorse start) omitted for lack of detail. Pitch 6 and 7 grades are contested between sources, so the ranges are stated and the notes say so. No rappel table: descent not found in sources read, and the route is not described as rappelled.
review.other_findings: Mountaineers lists it as 6 pitches; Wenatchee Outdoors counts 7 including the Remorse start. Stored row has no descent.

pitch_detail.notes: Knobby climbing up past several bolts to the top of a pillar, where the belay is. Getting started off the ground is the hardest part.
Step across the gap from the pillar onto the main wall. The crux comes in the first few bolts; reports place it either below the second bolt or past the third. Belay on a ledge.
A very airy traverse over to the third anchors, about 60 ft, ending at the base of an arete. Pitches 2 and 3 link well, which keeps the leader in sight of the belayer.
A few exciting moves up the arete, then veer right and follow an edge with the ground dropping away below. Often called the hardest pitch of the route.
Easy greenish slab (about 5.4) toward a short headwall; the headwall is rated 5.8 by one account and the pitch is easier than the ones below. Pitches 4 and 5 can be linked with a 70 m rope.

rappel_detail.station: Fixed anchor on the back (west) side of the formation, on a low-angle slab facing northwest.
rappel_detail.notes: The first rappel lands at the top of the third pitch.
hazards: Do not rappel from the pitch 5 anchors: a party did that, jammed their rope and needed rescue.

rappel_detail.station: Continue down the west side of the formation.
rappel_detail.notes: Single-rope rappel; a 60 m rope is recommended.

rappel_detail.station: Continue down the west side of the formation.
rappel_detail.notes: Last single-rope rappel to the ground.

Rappel table is thin: the count of three single-rope raps and the first landing at the top of pitch 3 come from descriptions on neighbouring routes' pages, so lengths and per-station detail were left out. Lengths and bolt counts omitted (not stated).
review.other_findings: Stored descent says rappel off the back to a fixed anchor; another account says a walk-off from the Smith Rock Group exists without rappelling.

pitch_detail.notes: Start straight up (5.5) or from the easier left side (5.3) to a ledge, then climb a flake system with angular blocks to the anchor, roughly 50 ft.

A long rightward traverse along a natural weakness, clipping three fixed pins. One slightly tricky 5.6 move is the mental crux for many; protect the second carefully. About 70 ft; can be linked with pitch 1.
Up slabs to a flake leading into a short chimney, exiting onto a ledge. About 70 ft.

The longest and best pitch, about 130 ft: follow the crack system to a small overhang, then layback up a flake (the 5.6 crux) to tree anchors. A short scramble over roots and dirt reaches the large ledge used for the walk-off.

review.changed: Pitch data from a search summary of a SummitPost description (page fetch blocked). That description lists 5 pitches (the 5th a scramble), merged into pitch 4's note to match the stored count of 4. Anchor on P2 given as bolts only because the source says bolt anchor without a count. review.other_findings: A different Thin Air exists at Smith Rock (the SummitPost id 157786/157818 pages are mixed up in search); the details above are the Cathedral Ledge route. Stored beta says first pitch roughly 50 ft to a piton-equipped stance while the source says a two-bolt anchor; anchors may have changed.

pitch_detail.notes: First pitch of the three-pitch direct start added with the free ascent, replacing the two blocky 5.8 pitches of the original line.
The physical and mental crux of the direct start: a sporty, gear-protected traverse to reach a steep hand crack.
Third pitch of the direct start, rejoining the original line.

review.changed: Only the direct start is documented in what I could read (search summary of the AAJ report; fetch blocked). Upper pitches omitted. No rappels: the route is a walk-off.
review.other_findings: The AAJ report calls the original A2 pitch nine (now 5.10+) a steep bouldery dihedral, while the stored overview names P8 (5.10 hand crack) as the money pitch; numbering may differ between the report and the stored text. Stored grade 5.10+ and length (1,230 ft is about 375 m) agree with the report.
